idea.title: Example listing: still photos vs a 15-second video
idea.angle: Using one example listing: the plain photo post, then the 15-second video made from the same photos with a hook, a short tour and one clear ask. Text-only before/after (captions, post layouts, first lines), no house photos.
idea.hook: SAME LISTING. PHOTOS VS A 15-SECOND VIDEO.

slides.heading: SAME LISTING. PHOTOS VS A **15-SECOND** VIDEO.
A 4-BED **FAMILY** HOME
slides.body: An example listing: garden, pool, quiet street. Same photos in both versions.

slides.heading: THE **FIRST** THING BUYERS SEE
slides.body:
Before: The front gate. No text.
After:
✓ The pool, moving slowly
✓ "4-bed with pool, quiet street" in bold

slides.heading: FROM PHOTO DUMP TO **TOUR**
slides.body:
Before: Twenty photos in random order.
After:
✓ Living room, kitchen, master bedroom
✓ Garden and pool to finish
✓ Two to three seconds each

slides.heading: FROM "DM FOR INFO" TO ONE **ASK**
slides.body:
Before: "DM for more info and price."
After:
✓ Price and area on screen
✓ "DM TOUR to book a viewing"

slides.heading: READABLE WITH THE **SOUND** OFF
slides.body:
Before: No text. Music only.
After:
✓ Big captions in brand colours
✓ Calm music that fits the home

slides.heading: SAME PHOTOS. NEW **PACKAGING**.
slides.body: Nothing was reshot. Nothing fake was added. The home just got easier to notice.

slides.heading: TURN PHOTOS INTO **VIDEO**
slides.body: Comment LISTING and I'll send you the playbook

caption:
Same example listing. Same photos. Two very different posts.

Before: twenty still photos, the gate first, "DM for more info."
After: a 15-second video with a bold hook on the best shot, a short tour of the main rooms and one clear ask.
Nothing was reshot. Nothing fake was added.
Short videos reach far more people than photo posts.

Which version would you stop scrolling for?

Comment LISTING and I'll send you the playbook.
